📌 Flash Loans: Borrowing Without Collateral for One Transaction

Main Points
⏺ A flash loan lets you borrow assets without collateral if repayment happens in the same transaction
⏺ If the loan isn’t repaid, the whole transaction reverts
⏺ This post explains why flash loans are useful — and why they often appear in exploit stories

1️⃣ Core Idea — you borrow assets, use them across several steps, and repay before the transaction ends.
2️⃣ Use Cases — arbitrage, position refinancing, liquidations, and complex DeFi strategies.
3️⃣ Why No Collateral — the lender doesn’t take time risk: if repayment fails, execution fails.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — flash loans can amplify oracle attacks, thin-pool manipulation, and weak protocol logic.
5️⃣ Practical Lens — the tool isn’t “bad,” but if one burst of temporary capital can break a protocol, the design is fragile.

Final Thoughts

A flash loan is credit for one blockchain breath. Safe for the lender, but a hammer against weak protocols.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Real Volume, Real Fees (Not "Farm Token" Emissions)

This is what makes Gala Swap different. The yield isn't based on inflationary "farm token" emissions that you have to constantly race against.

The LP rewards on Gala Swap are generated by real trading activity—the essential work of keeping the DEX price in sync with the broader market. When you provide liquidity, you become the infrastructure that makes this flow possible, and you earn your share of the fees from that volume.

The Real Gold Rush: Expanding the Surface

The current volume is impressive, but here’s what’s truly exciting: the bottleneck isn't the demand from traders; it's the surface area available for the arbitrage engine to work across.

A few dozen pools can only capture a few dozen tokens' worth of flow. Imagine this same efficient arbitrage engine running across hundreds of pools that simply don't exist yet.

The Takeaway:

The traders are ready. The volume is real. The arbitrage engine is already running. What's missing is the liquidity to serve that volume and capture those fees across a much broader range of pairs.

This is the official version of victory: missiles did the talking, diplomats kept the phone lines open, and the unnamed “senior leadership” decided when either tool would be used. Araghchi did not need to name Mojtaba Khamenei. The title did the work for him. 

A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran has moved from a defensive posture to a “fully offensive” one. The United States has a few weeks to implement the memorandum in full. Iran will communicate the timetable through mediators, prepare for escalation in Hormuz and the wider region, and consider a “timely and precise” strike to break the U.S. naval blockade if diplomacy fails. 

Tehran says that pressure on Washington and reliance on mediators cannot produce a permanent settlement. Yet it will use the same mediators to transmit its deadline. The channel survives. Confidence in what the channel can deliver does not.

The Wall Street Journal reports that Iran’s hard-line leadership used the pause under the memorandum to prepare for a longer war. 

The Revolutionary Guard is expanding its authority over the regular military, tightening domestic counterintelligence, promoting battle-hardened veterans, and accelerating missile and drone production. The ceasefire became a rearmament window. 

NBC News reports that Moscow is sending drone components, ammunition and TNT across the Caspian Sea to replenish Iranian stocks damaged in U.S. and Israeli strikes. 

Russia is helping Iran rearm while both governments continue to describe their partnership as deeply respectful of other people’s sovereignty. 

China has chosen the language of principle. Its ambassador in Tehran condemned what he called illegal U.S. and Israeli actions against Iran and set out four Chinese initiatives for regional peace and stability.

Iran’s next move will not be decided by an initiative. It will be decided by how quickly Tehran can rebuild its missiles, drones and confidence that the next round will cost its enemies more than the last one.

📣 EU to revise MiCA rules in 2027 amid US stablecoin push 

⚠️ European Union officials are preparing to revise the bloc’s MiCA crypto framework in 2027 as foreign stablecoin restrictions and faster U.S. rulemaking expose gaps in the existing regime. The planned revision would examine how MiCA treats stablecoins issued outside the European Union. Current requirements have prevented several foreign issuers from receiving authorization, limiting their access to regulated exchanges across the bloc.

💬 “Reopening the file seems unavoidable at this stage,” an unidentified European diplomat told Euronews.

🔗 The diplomat cited positions taken by European institutions, including the European Central Bank, along with changes in global regulation and digital-asset technology. No final proposal has been published. Any amendment would need to pass through the EU’s legislative process before taking effect. The consultation covers developments that have occurred since MiCA entered into application. Its deadline has been extended to Sept. 30, with crypto issuers, service providers, regulators, central banks and finance ministries invited to respond.

📉 More accounts. Fewer crypto trades

eToro’s latest results reveal an unusual split between user growth and trading activity.
The platform ended the second quarter with 4.28 million funded accounts, an increase of 18% year over year.

But its July crypto figures moved in the opposite direction:
• crypto trades fell 73% year over year to 1.4 million
• the average amount invested per crypto trade declined 50% to $182

At the same time, eToro reported that its overall number of trades remained flat, with equities helping drive the company’s growth.

The conclusion is not that users are abandoning financial platforms.
It is that account growth and crypto activity are two different signals.

A larger user base does not automatically create more trades. Participation depends on market conditions, volatility, confidence and whether investors see enough opportunity to act.

Registrations measure access.
Trading activity measures conviction.
In the current market, the distance between the two remains significant.
